approved: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2019

The majority voted against an [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2019-09-11.18.1) to the usual [second reading motion](https://www.peo.gov.au/learning/fact-sheets/making-a-law.html) "*that the bills be read a second time*", which is parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill. Since this vote was unsuccessful, the second reading motion will remain unchanged. ### Amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House calls on the Government to implement a plan for a large-scale carbon capture and storage plan to help Australia meet its international emissions targets while further growing Australia's resources sector".*

The amendment called for a large-scale carbon capture and storage plan, arguing that Australia’s emissions rose 0.6% in the year to March 2019, existing projects like Gorgon, CarbonNet, and COAL21 store less than 10 million tonnes annually against a 2030 budget of 440 million tonnes, and the government provides no carbon price or policy framework to bridge the $40 per tonne cost gap.

The speaker supported the amendment and the bills to transfer regulatory oversight of offshore greenhouse gas storage wells to NOPSEMA, strengthening its powers to inspect and enforce compliance, including warrantless entry to contractors and integrity inspections, and noted the Gorgon Project on Barrow Island as the world's largest carbon capture and storage project.

The Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2019 transfers regulatory oversight of offshore greenhouse storage, environmental management and well operations to NOPSEMA, strengthens NOPSEMA inspectors’ powers, and introduces enforceable undertakings. The Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Amendment Bill 2019 extends well-related levies to greenhouse gas titles to allow NOPSEMA to recover costs for overseeing well operations under those titles.
